observation.visible_scene: An overcast outdoor park lawn. A person stands at the left edge holding a bubble wand, a white bucket sits on the grass nearby, and a wooden gazebo stands at the right beneath large trees, with a baseball backstop and red houses in the left background. Several iridescent soap bubbles of varying size float in the air, the largest one occupying the center of the frame.
visible_changes: The large central bubble slowly translates rightward across the clip (its center shifts from roughly mid-frame toward the right) while its membrane continuously undulates and changes outline shape, indicating deformation as well as drift.
Two smaller bubbles in the left-center area (near the wand/bucket) appear and grow during the segment, then drift rightward at low height, changing shape as they move.
An elongated yellowish bubble in the upper-right region drifts slowly rightward and slightly upward, its form stretching and reshaping.
The bubbles near the gazebo on the right shift position gradually, moving rightward and outward.
The person, bucket, trees, backstop, houses and gazebo remain fixed in place; the camera viewpoint is static (background landmarks do not pan or zoom).
outside_clip_unknowns: How the large bubble was formed and whether the wand is still connected to it.
What happens to the bubbles after the clip ends (pop, land, or continue drifting).
Whether additional bubbles are produced by the person before or after this segment.
uncertain_details: The exact instant each small bubble detaches from the wand is not clearly resolved.
The thin curved line near the right edge of the large bubble could be a wand/string or a bubble edge; its nature is unclear.
It is uncertain whether the upper-right yellowish bubble originated from the large bubble or is a separate bubble already in flight.
